issue.title: res.render()/app.render() throws opaque TypeError for a view name ending in "."

relevant_locations.role: Initializes View extension and handles default engine fallback logic where extname('.') incorrectly triggers valid extension handling.
Loads template engine using `this.ext.slice(1)`, which evaluates to `''` when `this.ext` is `'.'`, causing `require('')`.

llm_context.input_body: No body provided in issue description.

generated_output.summary: When a view name ends with a dot (e.g., 'index.'), path.extname() returns '.' which is truthy. This causes Express to skip its default engine fallback mechanism, leaving the extension as '.' and attempting to call require('') when loading the view module, resulting in a synchronous TypeError.
generated_output.root_cause_analysis: The View constructor in `lib/view.js` uses `path.extname(name)` to determine if an extension was explicitly provided. For a string like `'index.'`, `path.extname()` returns `'.'` instead of an empty string or a valid extension. Express interprets this truthy single-dot extension as valid, fails to find a matching template engine for `'.'`, tries to load module `''`, and throws a Node.js runtime TypeError.

step_by_step_plan.title: Inspect View extension logic in lib/view.js
step_by_step_plan.description: Inspect the constructor of View in lib/view.js where path.extname(name) is used to check for an extension, and observe how a trailing dot results in ext equal to '.' which bypasses the default engine fallback check (!this.ext).

step_by_step_plan.title: Validate extension string in View constructor
step_by_step_plan.description: Modify the extension assignment or check in lib/view.js so that if path.extname(name) results in exactly '.', it is treated as an empty string (no extension) rather than a valid extension.

step_by_step_plan.title: Ensure fallback handles trailing dot view names correctly
step_by_step_plan.description: Verify that when ext is normalized or ignored when it equals '.', the default engine lookup triggers correctly and leads to a graceful 'Failed to lookup view' error callback instead of throwing a synchronous TypeError.

step_by_step_plan.title: Add regression test for view names ending with a dot
step_by_step_plan.description: Add a new test case in the test suite (e.g., within view-related tests) that attempts to render or lookup a view with a trailing dot (e.g. 'index.') and asserts that it passes an error to the callback instead of throwing a synchronous TypeError.

step_by_step_plan.title: Run test suite to verify fix
step_by_step_plan.description: Run the repository test command to ensure the regression test passes and no existing view rendering tests are broken.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: Handling special characters and edge cases (like trailing dots) when using `path.extname()`.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Functions like `path.extname()` can return unexpected results on malformed input strings, which can corrupt subsequent control flow if not properly validated.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: A trailing dot causes `path.extname()` to return `'.'` rather than an empty string, tricking Express into thinking a file extension was supplied.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: Validating dynamic module names before passing them to the Node.js `require()` function.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Passing empty or invalid strings to `require()` throws synchronous runtime errors that can bypass error-handling callbacks and crash applications.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: Express attempts to `require(mod)` where `mod` is an empty string derived from `this.ext.slice(1)`, resulting in a synchronous TypeError instead of invoking the callback with an error.

common_pitfalls: Assuming `path.extname()` always returns a non-empty extension string whenever it is truthy.
Allowing synchronous exceptions to escape out of `app.render()` instead of safely capturing them or passing them to the callback.
